title: Bash readonly auto-allow: tree -H --houtro dumps absolute file contents
description: tree is COMMAND_ALLOWLIST-readonly with --houtro allowed as a string file path, but tree is not a PathCommand so absolute host paths bypass checkPathConstraints. At bashPermissions step 7, BashTool.isReadOnly auto-allows the command. With -H (HTML mode), tree embeds the outro file body verbatim into stdout HTML. Distinct from already-filed tree --hintro.
evidence: PoC: tree -H . --houtro=/tmp/dummy_creds.txt <dir> → stdout HTML contains API_KEY= and PASSWORD= lines from dummy file; harness step7AutoAllow=true
remediation: Remove --houtro (and --hintro) from tree.safeFlags, or add tree to PATH_EXTRACTORS and validate --houtro/--hintro file operands against the working-directory allowlist.

title: Bash readonly auto-allow: tree --fromfile dumps absolute file lines
description: tree --fromfile is allowlisted as a no-arg flag; the following positional path is the file whose lines are printed as tree node names. tree is not a PathCommand, so absolute paths passthrough path validation and are auto-allowed at step 7. Distinct from already-filed --fromtabfile (different flag/parser).
evidence: PoC: tree --fromfile /tmp/dummy_creds.txt prints each credential line as a tree leaf; harness step7AutoAllow=true (fused --fromfile=/abs rejected)
remediation: Remove --fromfile/--fromtabfile from tree.safeFlags, or extract and path-validate the operand file for those modes.
